name: arXiv API entry for 2510.09665 (LMCache v1/v2) - submission date makes an ICLR 2025 acceptance impossible
notes:
THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT against paper-lmcache's venue=iclr, and it is arithmetic rather than an index search, which is why it survives the objection that any venue index could be incomplete.
The arXiv API returns for 2510.09665: published 2025-10-08T00:15:04Z, updated 2025-12-05T04:52:54Z (v2). ICLR 2025 author notifications were January 2025 and its conference was April 2025; ICLR 2026's cycle is the next one open after this preprint appeared. A paper first posted to arXiv in OCTOBER 2025 therefore cannot have been an ICLR 2025 paper - the decision preceded the preprint by roughly nine months. The only conference venues still reachable by a first-submission date of October 2025 are late-2025 and 2026 venues.
This is a stronger form of evidence than a negative index search because it does not depend on the index being complete: it is a consistency argument between two dates that are independently documented. It also explains HOW the error got in. The repo's own source record pap-sys-lmcache-openreview states 'content.venue = 'ICLR 2025 Poster'' for a URL that is an api2 SEARCH query rather than a specific forum, and pap-sys-lmcache-arxiv repeats it - a claim of an exact venue string with no forum id behind it, on a search URL that returns a different venue when queried today. Wave 4 flagged the paper contested on the strength of re-running that search; this source explains what the original claim was resting on.
The same query also supplies the abstract facts that make the record worth keeping: LMCACHE is described as 'the first and so far the most efficient open-source KV caching solution', extracts and shares KV caches across vLLM and SGLang, supports both cache offloading (prefix reuse across queries) and PD disaggregation (cross-engine cache transfer), and reports up to 15x throughput improvement when combined with vLLM on multi-round QA and document analysis. arXiv comment field is empty.
